title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 77-79). Grothendieck is building a rigidified, 'pinned' description of elliptic curves over a base of residue characteristic ≠ 2 (absolute base S0 = Spec Z[1/2]). The ingredients are as follows.

- A three-element étale set J. Presumably this is E[2] minus 0, i.e. the three finite branch points of the quotient E → E/±1.
- Objects canonically attached to J: Σ_J, the projective line containing J; Σ_J^* = Σ_J minus J, a twisted λ-line U_{0,3}; and D_J.
- ω_J, a two-element set, i.e. a μ2-torsor, intrinsically attached to J.
- μ4^* = μ4 minus μ2 = {i, −i}, viewed as a μ2-torsor over S0, i.e. the quadratic étale cover Spec Z[1/2, i].

On the previous page he fixes a 'square' Q0. This is a μ4-torsor with Aut^+(Q0) ≅ μ4^*-data. It is very plausibly the harmonic quadruple / square lattice attached to j = 1728, whose automorphism group is μ4. An iso ω_{Q0} ≅ μ4^* is rewritten, via D_{Q0} ≅ μ4^* (19), as the datum (20) α: ω_J ≅ μ4^*. Since μ2-torsors are self-dual, such an α is a section of the contracted product ω_J ∧^{μ2} μ4^*.

This page then states two things.

(1) A Legendre pinning. The groupoid of elliptic curves over k with a 'Legendre pinning' is equivalent to the groupoid of triples (J, t, α). Here J is a 3-element set, t ∈ Σ_J^*(k) is the position of the fourth branch point (the image of the origin) relative to J, and α: ω_J ≅ μ4^* is an 'arithmetic' datum. This α is what kills the ±1 / quadratic-twist ambiguity: the λ-invariant determines (E, level-2 structure) only up to quadratic twist.

(2) A Legendre-Jacobi pinning of level 2. This adds a Jacobi (full level-2) pinning, a bijection J ≅ {0, 1, ∞}. That identifies Σ_J with P^1_k and Σ_J^* with U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0, 1, ∞}. It makes ω_J ≅ ω_{{0,1,∞}} trivial with a privileged element ω^+. Datum (c) then reduces to the choice of a square root i of −1, the 'arithmetic' datum. The resulting groupoid is rigid (no non-identity automorphisms). On the next page it is identified with the set of pairs (t, i), t ∈ U_{0,3}(k), i ∈ μ4^*(k).

In modern terms: the stack of elliptic curves with full level-2 structure plus this extra 'Legendre' rigidification is represented by the scheme U_{0,3} ×_{S0} μ4^*, i.e. the λ-line over Z[1/2, i]. The ±1 automorphism is killed by the μ2-torsor datum. The next page then introduces the twisting operation M ↦ M^♮ = M ∧^{μ4} Q0 and M^♭ = M ∧^{μ2} μ4^*, to handle descent from Z[1/2, i] to Z[1/2]. The whole serves a fine-moduli / 'anabelian-style' arithmetic description of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, in terms of explicit torsors under μ2 and μ4.
errors: No outright mathematical error is visible. A consequence worth flagging: once the Jacobi pinning trivializes ω_J, the datum α amounts to an element of μ4^*(k). So Legendre-Jacobi-pinned curves exist over k only if √−1 ∈ k, and the representing scheme lives over Z[1/2, i], not Z[1/2]. This differs from the classical Legendre family y² = x(x−1)(x−λ) over Z[1/2][λ, 1/(λ(1−λ))], so Grothendieck's 'épinglage de Legendre' is not literally the Katz–Mazur Legendre structure. The precise definitions of ω_J and D_J are on earlier pages and cannot be checked here.

The page is a draft: the final sentence is cancelled and restarted. The rigidity claim (no non-identity automorphisms) is asserted without proof. It is plausible because −1 acts nontrivially on the α-datum or the pinning.

ideas.what: Describing elliptic curves with level-2 data as triples (J, t, α): a 3-point set J, a point t of the twisted λ-line Σ_J^* = Σ_J minus J, and a μ2-torsor isomorphism α: ω_J ≅ μ4^*
ideas.modern_name: Rigidified level-2 moduli; λ-line as fine moduli after killing the μ2 automorphism gerbe (twisting datum)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre family classical; moduli-theoretic treatment by Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport (1973), Katz–Mazur (1985, Legendre moduli problem)

ideas.what: Legendre-Jacobi pinning of level 2: J ≅ {0, 1, ∞} plus a choice of √−1. The groupoid is rigid and equivalent to U_{0,3}(k) × μ4^*(k)
ideas.modern_name: Fine moduli scheme for Γ(2)-structure plus extra arithmetic rigidification, λ-line over Z[1/2, i]

ideas.what: Treating μ4^* = μ4 minus μ2 as a μ2-torsor (the quadratic étale cover Spec Z[1/2, i] of Spec Z[1/2]) and isolating it as the 'arithmetic' part of the pinning; twisting by the μ4-torsor Q0 (attached to the square / j = 1728)
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by torsors / contracted products; Galois descent from Z[1/2, i]
ideas.where_published: General torsor and contracted-product formalism is in SGA 1/SGA 3 and Giraud; this specific application is not published

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an intrinsic, torsor-theoretic 'épinglage' formalism for level-2 moduli in characteristic ≠ 2. In it the obstruction to descending the λ-line description from Z[1/2, i] to Z[1/2] is isolated as an explicit μ2-torsor datum ω_J ∧ μ4^*, tied to the j = 1728 square Q0. This canonical-twisting viewpoint seems not to have been written up. It is close in spirit to, but distinct from, the Katz–Mazur Legendre moduli problem.
missed.quote: la donnée c) de l'épinglage par Legendre équivaut donc à celle d'une racine carrée de -1, soit i — c'est la donnée "arithmétique"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest interest. It gives an intrinsic accounting of the arithmetic (Gal(Q(i)/Q)) part of the Γ(2) / Legendre tower, relevant to Galois actions on the first levels of the M_{1,1} Teichmüller tower (Esquisse programme). But the underlying mathematics is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful but standard reformulation of Legendre and level-2 structures as fine moduli via torsor data. The specific 'Legendre-Jacobi épinglage' packaging and the isolation of √−1 as the arithmetic datum are unpublished details. They are not substantively new relative to Igusa / Deligne–Rapoport / Katz–Mazur.
transcription_corrections: The equation label at top is (20), not (2θ).
'le donné d'une groupe d'épinglage' should read 'la donnée d'un couple d'épinglages' (one Legendre, one Jacobi of level 2).
'Un épinglage de Legendre-Jacobi d'échelon 2 d'une courbe elliptique E [est] la donnée…': the inserted phrase 'd'une courbe elliptique E' replaces a cancelled phrase.
'courbes elliptiques/k épinglées par Legendre [sont] équivalente[s]': a cancelled word precedes 'équivalente'.
The margin insert reads '(est rigide (pas d'auto. non identiques))', with 'non identiques' possibly struck. The struck tail is 'équivalente à celles des objets : isom. près'.
Item c) reads 'd'un isom α : ω_J ≃ μ4^* (= μ4^*(k))'. The struck symbol after μ4^* is a deletion.
